FINAL ANSWER

**Merge rule used (submitted):** a single, global convex blend of the two fine-tuning deltas applied uniformly to every backbone tensor (all 150 tensors except the two heads):

    W = P + 0.40·(W_cifar − P) + 0.60·(W_cub − P)

i.e. for each key, `sd[k] = parent[k] + 0.40·δc[k] + 0.60·δu[k]`, computed in float64 and cast back to float32. No per-layer or per-tensor-type weighting, no scaling beyond the (0.40, 0.60) split.

**Why this rule (weight-space analysis, no labels used):**
- The two fine-tuning deltas δc, δu are **nearly orthogonal** at every depth: per-block cosine 0.12–0.18 in the earliest blocks and 0.02–0.06 in mid/late blocks (only the final LayerNorm, 0.97, and the class token, 0.74, are aligned). So the two adaptations occupy almost disjoint parameter directions and a convex blend is the natural compromise — there is no "shared" component worth averaging first.
- CIFAR's delta is consistently ~1.5× larger in norm than CUB's at every block (rel. size ≈0.19–0.24 vs 0.13–0.17 of the parent norm), so the equal-weight blend over-weights CIFAR's perturbation and starves CUB; this predicted an optimum shifted toward the CUB delta, confirmed by measurement.
- The two fixed heads read feature subspaces that overlap **exactly at the random baseline** (‖W_cub·proj_row(W_cifar)‖ / ‖W_cub‖ = 0.361 = √(100/768)), so there is no head-aware subspace trick available; the only real freedom is the global mixing ratio.
- Everything more elaborate was tested and lost: adding both full deltas (a=b=1 → CUB collapses to 42.7, total perturbation scale matters), mild scale-up (0.41/0.77 → 79.3), and depth-dependent ratio tilts in both directions (tilt toward CUB late: 78.7; tilt toward CIFAR late: 79.8). Uniform convex blending at total scale 1 is the optimum of this family, and the measured accuracy curve is concave with its vertex between t=0.55 and 0.65.

**Practice accuracies measured (CIFAR-100 / CUB / mean):**
- **Submitted: a=0.40, b=0.60 → 82.40 / 78.30 / 80.35**
- a=0.35, b=0.65 → 80.32 / 79.93 / 80.13
- reference average (a=b=0.5) → 85.20 / 74.09 / 79.64
- a=0.30, b=0.70 → 77.98 / 81.22 / 79.60
- depth ramps: CIFAR-heavy late 79.92 / 79.62 / 79.77; CUB-heavy late 78.88 / 78.57 / 78.73
- a=0.41, b=0.77 (scale-up) → 79.46 / 79.06 / 79.26
- a=0.20, b=0.80 → 72.02 / 83.03 / 77.52
- sum of both deltas → 77.14 / 42.71 / 59.93
- single children (reference): 88.38 / 22.02 / 55.20 and 51.06 / 84.14 / 67.60

So the merge beats the "average" baseline by about **+0.7 points mean** (80.35 vs 79.64), with a much more balanced profile than either child backbone alone.
